item.title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.
item.dc:creator: Peng Liu, Dong Xie

item.title: Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.29017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Dittmer

item.title: Weak Relative Calabi-Yau Structures for Legendrian Contact Homology
item.description: arXiv:2509.02485v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Legendrian Contact Homology (LCH) and its augmentations are important invariants of Legendrian submanifolds, and for Legendrian knots in the standard contact 3-space in particular. We increase understanding of the algebraic structure of LCH by generalizing the duality isomorphism and long exact sequence for linearized LCH for Legendrian knots to a weak relative Calabi-Yau structure for $A_\infty$ bimodules over the positive augmentation category.
item.dc:creator: Jiajie Ma, Joshua M. Sabloff

item.title: Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles under Weak Index Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles. Building on the existing multiplicity result Theorem 1.3 for closed Reeb orbits on prequantization $S^1$-bundles, we weaken the index assumptions by requiring only that the supporting contact form has no contractible periodic Reeb orbits with mean Conley-Zehnder index zero and no contractible good periodic Reeb orbits with Conley-Zehnder index 0, and we obtain a lower bound for the number of geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits carried by contact forms $\alpha$ on a prequantization $S^1$-bundle under certain natural topological assumptions (Theorem 1.6). In dimension five we further relax the index assumptions and show that, under a mild index condition imposed only on simple contractible periodic orbits and the same topological assumptions on the prequantization $S^1$-bundle, every non-degenerate supporting contact form carries at least $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits (Theorem 1.11), in agreement with the conjectural lower bound for prequantization bundles.
item.dc:creator: Peng Liu, Dong Xie

item.title: Port-Hamiltonian systems with energy and power ports
item.description: arXiv:2405.01241v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the port-Hamiltonian framework defined with respect to a Lagrangian submanifold and a Dirac structure by augmenting the Lagrangian submanifold with the space of external variables. The new pair of conjugated variables is called energy port. We show that in the most general case, the extension describes constrained Hamiltonian systems whose Hamiltonian function depends on inputs.
item.dc:creator: Kaja Krhac, Bernhard Maschke, Arjan van der Schaft

item.title: From BV-BFV Quantization to Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2604.04556v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a program for bridging the gap between the perturbative BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory and the non-perturbative Reshetikhin-Turaev (RT) invariants of 3-manifolds, passing through factorization homology of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras and the derived algebraic geometry of character stacks. We conjecture that the modular tensor category underlying the RT construction arises as the $\mathbb{E}_2$-category from BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory on the disk, with the derived character stack $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_\mathbb{C}}(\Sigma)$ of the complexified group and its shifted symplectic structure mediating the proposed identification. A recurring theme is the mismatch between the compact gauge group of Chern-Simons theory and the reductive algebraic group of derived algebraic geometry: we work throughout with $G_\mathbb{C}$ and indicate where a Riemann-Hilbert type comparison is needed to return to the compact theory. We formulate a main conjecture asserting natural equivalence of the BV-BFV and RT constructions as 3-2-1-extended topological quantum field theories, together with several auxiliary conjectures and two questions, develop a proof strategy via deformation quantization of shifted symplectic stacks, and clarify the role of $\mathbb{E}_n$-Koszul duality, which relates the perturbative expansion around a flat connection to the local geometry of the character stack. We relate the perturbative expansions to the sheaf of vanishing cycles on the character stack of a $3$-manifold, propose that a stratification of the character stack by stabilizer type organizes the trans-series decomposition, and propose that the Stokes data of the perturbative expansion should be read as a stability datum in the sense of Kontsevich-Soibelman, with the Chern-Simons functional playing the role of the central charge.
item.dc:creator: Nima Moshayedi
